reviewer: implementation worker — code-grounded unit, fail-closed cache lifecycle, route-complete real-browser evidence; independent review remains required
summary: Canonical Turkish BERT NER runs through raw ORT-Web with exact length+SHA-256 verification before use/cache and on cache hits. Pinned XLM-R language ID and the full route ladder passed 37/37 fail-closed assertions across 10 route/device cells and 20 populated full-page theme captures, plus two mosaics. Every sample/field/toggle/copy/details/release/clear workflow and the supported lifecycle matrix is retained.

rubric.evidence: Raw browser preflight proves canonical logits; schema-2 acceptance-run.json binds the current implementation commit and records 37/37 assertions with real output on all five routes at desktop/mobile and light/dark.
rubric.notes: No multilingual NER substitute is used. Multi-model adds language identification but the entity stage remains the canonical akdeniz27 model.

rubric.evidence: Browser logits are [1, WordPieces, 7]. 'Elif Şafak, Boğaziçi Üniversitesi'nde Ahmet Hamdi Tanpınar…' produced PER Elif Şafak 99%, ORG Boğaziçi Üniversitesi 100%, PER Ahmet Hamdi Tanpınar 100%; Tan + ##pınar is exposed raw then aligned to one word/span.
rubric.notes: The exact original-character offsets drive highlighting, JSON export, redaction and story recasting.

rubric.evidence: Primary pins revision 99995f7d… with fp32 model.onnx 440,394,743 bytes/SHA-256 a8f8a685…4482 and verifies both before persistence/use and on every hit. Language ID pins revision 919c87aa… with q8 model_quantized.onnx 278,836,241 bytes/SHA-256 e3a2f1b4…182c9; acceptance observed both exact pinned request lengths.
rubric.notes: The canonical repo has no Transformers.js onnx/model_*.onnx layout, so the raw ORT path is deliberate and inspectable.

rubric.evidence: Every route uses createModelLoader. Acceptance proves absent→blocked failure→Retry→ready, current cached auto-init, SHA-verified offline cached inference, eviction→partial/Re-download, poisoned cache rejection/deletion→Retry, and both Clear controls returning to absent.
rubric.notes: Primary bytes cross the cache boundary only after exact length+SHA verification; immutable Update and WASM feature-unsupported are honestly N/A.

rubric.evidence: acceptance-run.json retains first visit, network error/Retry, cached reload, two in-flight disposal races, offline cached inference, partial eviction recovery, corrupt cache fail-closed recovery, release/reload, and clear-to-absent. Mutable Update and feature-gated unsupported are explicitly N/A with reasons.
rubric.notes: The page warns about storage and roughly 1–1.5 GiB transient memory before download.

rubric.evidence: Both desktop and mobile drive four overview examples, four Basics examples, Practical JSON/redaction copies and PER/ORG/LOC toggles, all three Wild samples and every replacement field, Turkish/English/code-switched language cases, every details disclosure, and both model Release/Clear controls.
rubric.notes: All visible controls are native elements with names; controls disable when their worker is released.

rubric.evidence: No entity arrays are embedded in UI source. The validator changes input and observes discriminating live spans: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk/Ankara/Türkiye Cumhuriyeti; Elif Şafak/Boğaziçi Üniversitesi/Ahmet Hamdi Tanpınar; practical spans and code-switched language routing.

All 10 route/device cells report zero unnamed buttons and zero sub-44px non-checkbox controls. Native controls, labelled Turkish inputs, visible text labels, live status regions, and every details disclosure are exercised.
rubric.notes: Twenty populated full-page light/dark screenshots and two mosaics are committed with content-hash provenance for independent review.

rubric.evidence: 10/10 route/device cells (1280×800 desktop, 360×740 DPR3 mobile) and 20/20 light/dark full-page captures report horizontal overflow 0, no clipped/small controls, and zero post-recovery console/network failures. Outputs and lower controls are visibly retained.
rubric.notes: Responsive UX is supported on mobile, while the page honestly says whether a particular phone can afford the 420 MiB download/runtime memory is device-dependent.

rubric.evidence: Tokenizer/session/inference/alignment/BIO work remains in module workers. Client and workers implement latest-wins cancellation with one running + at most one queued job; unit and browser disposal-race evidence proves pending rejection and stale suppression.
rubric.notes: ORT session creation is heavy but off-main-thread; WASM is single-threaded for broad hosting compatibility.

guidanceConsulted.query: worker cancellation bounded queue stale response suppression model cache SHA-256 validation accessible lifecycle controls
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Move >250 ms computation off-main-thread, debounce rapid input, separate immediate UI state from worker computation, and cache deliberately.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: inference/integrity stays in workers; latest-wins cancellation bounds queues and suppresses stale output; only verified primary bytes are persisted.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: ner.js, worker.js, language-worker.js; test/turkish-ner.test.mjs; disposal-race acceptance records

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible native controls and responsive form targets
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use labelled native controls, visible focus/state, live errors, and at least 44–48px effective touch targets.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied without custom widgets; every field/toggle/copy/action is driven at desktop/mobile and route errors remain visible.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: 37/37 browser assertions; 10/10 cells have unnamedButtons=0 and smallControls=[]

guidanceConsulted.query: worker lifecycle controls status details keyboard accessibility
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer native semantics, centralized polite status, logical keyboard access, and test disclosures/controls rather than inferring support.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: native buttons/checkboxes/details, role=status, Turkish lang annotations, and every details disclosure opened and closed in acceptance.

openQuestions: Would an upstream faithful q8 export preserve enough NER quality to reduce the 420 MiB download substantially? It must be independently compared before replacing this canonical fp32 lineage.
How should real low-memory phones expose a pre-download storage/RAM capability estimate when browsers do not provide reliable available-RAM information?

followUpGoals.goal: If the canonical publisher releases a quantised ONNX, add an evidence-backed dtype choice only after span-level parity testing; do not silently replace fp32.
